Maria: Quick heads-up — new reranker bring-up (rk-3b-primed, int8 PTQ) shows mixed signals on the holdout.
Maria: NDCG improved ~+0.02 but MRR dropped ~-0.05. Low-level suspicion: candidate text normalization/serializer differences between offline eval and prod candidate pipeline.
Maria: Example diff that might matter:
```
old_serializer -> preserves trailing whitespace and HTML-escapes
  'How to bake bread '  
new_serializer -> trims and unescapes
  'How to bake bread'
```
Maria: Small difference, but it changes tokenization and tiebreakers in the reranker.
Kevin: Oof, that kind of drift can flip top1 a lot. Do we have the exact eval run ids + artifact hashes? can we diff the candidate files?
Maria: Eval run: run://2026-03-20/rk3b-int8-eval (artifact sha: ab12cd34). Prod candidate dump: s3://redwood-prod/candidates/2026-03-18/dump-46 (sha: f9e8d7c6).
Irene: Could also be subtle dedupe/order change — if two candidates collapse differently the MRR is sensitive. We should compare: normalizer(old) vs normalizer(new) on the same candidate set and check tokenized lengths + anchors.
Sam: Quick parity check I use locally: ``python -m rerank.tools.normalize_compare --a old_candidates.json --b new_candidates.json --out diffs.json`` — it prints example pairs where normalized text differs and tokenization mismatch counts.
Sam: Also run a top-k stability probe: rerank.eval --run runA --run runB --slice topk:1,3,5 to see where MRR diverges.
Maria: Running the normalize_compare now. Pasting first few diffs in a sec. @Kevin @Irene please watch the eval-bot job I kicked.
eval-bot: job run://2026-03-20/rk3b-int8-eval completed. metrics: NDCG@10: 0.743 -> 0.765, MRR@10: 0.512 -> 0.466. (delta ndcg +0.022, delta mrr -0.046)
Maria: normalize_compare found ~1.8% of candidates with whitespace-only diffs and ~0.4% with HTML-entity differences. Most are trailing/leading spaces and "&" vs "&".
Irene: That explains anchoring mismatches. Suggest normalization policy: trim, collapse internal whitespace to single space, html-unescape, then canonical-casefold. Add as a check in onboarding CI.
Kevin: I agree. Also add a small gating eval: run a fast sample (10k queries) and assert MRR delta < 0.01 or fail. If we catch normalization diffs early we avoid weird production flips.
Sam: I'll open a tiny PR to reranker-serving that pins the serializer to the canonical pipeline and add the parity script as a CI job.
Maria: Thanks — I'll re-run full eval after PR and post updated numbers here. If MRR still bad we'll dig into candidate ordering / dedupe heuristics next.
Kevin: :thumbsup: keep it high signal; love that we have small reproducible CLI checks.
Irene: Also file a quick incident note if PR rollout affected live traffic previously — just for audit.
Maria: Will do. Posting diffs: first examples in comments of the PR."
